body:
Retain the last good RCC source generation when a reload or package validation fails, so existing actions keep using their accepted source. Discard only newly created failed snapshots; keep reused generations until lease-safe collection is implemented. Runtime-executed test fixtures use the published Actions Core 1.0.2 interface.

Current checkpoint: `969219e7aa398f61b11466a2dc16ac3143568ff5`, tree `f139ebb38c943647c5e7c0bd6786b5d7c9385465`. The exact checkpoint is pushed and already contained in PR #273 at `6ece09c439d12e02bcbde9dcd2164956b97829e2`. Root owns admission into `integration/community-release-20261008`; no duplicate cherry-pick is needed.

The acceptance receipt captures the Runtime return code before any cleanup can consume child status. HTTP shutdown success and a natural exit are recorded separately from fallback process cleanup. A failed request, an unobserved exit, or a crash cannot become PASS because cleanup later returns zero.

Verification:

- Focused source-snapshot, failed-reload, and adapter checks: 70 passed / 2 real-RCC cases skipped. Root repeated that selection on the combined predecessor `31994384`; this is separate from hosted proof for the latest PR273 head.
- Independent review accepted the receipt correction and its fail-closed handling. The combined candidate's full Runtime, native, toolkit, installed-wheel and coverage checks remain authoritative for admission.
- The real RCC failed-reload probe on this checkpoint is **FAIL**: HTTP shutdown returned 200, then the Runtime exited naturally with `-11` before cleanup. A bounded faulthandler diagnostic reproduced a segmentation fault without a Python frame. Python 3.12.15 and psutil 5.9.8 were observed; neither is established as the cause. No native stack is available yet.

Retained original failing receipt SHA-256: `e79c93956477f95908eb0bd0efdd04339fd6afaa2178414cb2d57a1df1604813`; diagnostic receipt SHA-256: `507d26b9de81606a3cb3d49ab78f095412f1f9cee514a92200bc392ca73b7670`. Earlier cleanup-derived or older-source observations do not establish natural shutdown on this head.

This remains a blocked component of #134 and the PR273 convergence candidate. It does not establish Windows ACL behavior, strict-remote execution, complete descendant reaping, lease-safe generation collection, or full #134 acceptance. Do not admit this checkpoint solely from green targeted CI.

Documentation improvement: `docs/skills/repository-operations.md` documents source-generation retention, published fixture pins, and the distinction between natural exit and cleanup. Upstream disposition: cause and ownership of the crash remain unconfirmed; no upstream issue or speculative dependency change.
